body: # These options can keep to use single name import
# Defines the imports layout. The layout can be composed by the following symbols:
# "*" - wildcard. There must be at least one entry of a single wildcard to match all other imports. Matches anything after a specified symbol/import as well.
# "|" - blank line. Supports only single blank lines between imports. No blank line is allowed in the beginning or end of the layout.
# "^" - alias import, e.g. "^android.*" will match all android alias imports, "^" will match all other alias imports.
# import paths - these can be full paths, e.g. "java.util.List.*" as well as wildcard paths, e.g. "kotlin.**"
# Examples (we use ij_kotlin_imports_layout to set an imports layout for both ktlint and IDEA via a single property):
# ij_kotlin_imports_layout=* # alphabetical with capital letters before lower case letters (e.g. Z before a), no blank lines
# default IntelliJ IDEA style, same as alphabetical, but with "java", "javax", "kotlin" an  d alias imports in the end of the imports list
# According to https://kotlinlang.org/docs/reference/coding-conventions.html#names-for-test-methods it is acceptable to write method names
# in natural language. When using natural language, the description tends to be longer. Allow lines containing an identifier between
# backticks to be longer than the maximum line length. (Since 0.41.0)
# Comma-separated list of allowed wildcard imports that will override the no-wildcard-imports rule.
# This can be used for allowing wildcard imports from libraries like Ktor where extension functions are used in a way that creates a lot of imports.
# "**" applies to package and all subpackages
# ij_kotlin_packages_to_use_import_on_demand=io.ktor.** # allow wildcard import from io.ktor.* and all subpackages
# Manages dev tools like node, python, cmake, terraform, and hundreds more
# Like make, it manages tasks used to build and test projects
# mise_bin: String - Points to the path to the current mise executable
description="Setup the environment and install the tools"
# Pushes tools' bin-paths to the front of PATH instead of allowing modifications of PATH after activation to take precedence.
# Specific tools to enable idiomatic version files for like .node-version, .ruby-version, etc.
# Automatically install tools that are not installed
# Read/update lockfiles for tool versions. This is useful when you'd like to have loose versions in mise.tomlLockfile to use for the project.
# Change output style when executing tasks. This controls the output of mise run.
# Automatically install tools that are not installed when running tasks
# Config files with these prefixes will be trusted by default
# set to true to automatically answer yes to all prompts
# set to true to see full installation output, see `MISE_VERBOSE`
# path to the shorthands file, see `MISE_SHORTHANDS_FILE`
# Local settings override global ones (shallow merge). CLI flags override both.
# Top-level fields control Bun's core runtime behaviour.
# Scripts/plugins to execute before running a file or script.
# Use this to register Bun plugins globally.
# Useful for non-TypeScript projects that don't have a tsconfig.
# "react-jsxdev"    → automatic JSX runtime with dev warnings
# jsxFactory = "h"              # function used for JSX elements (classic only)
# Reduce memory usage at the cost of performance.
# Equivalent to setting DO_NOT_TRACK=1 in the environment.
# Set to false to rely solely on system environment variables.
# Explicit --env-file flags are always honoured regardless of this setting.
# file = false                  # same as above, object form
# Values are JSON strings; single-quoted strings and 'undefined' are also accepted.
# Map custom file extensions to Bun loaders.
# Supported loaders: jsx | js | ts | tsx | css | file | json | toml | wasm | napi | base64 | dataurl | text
depth = 2       # how deeply nested objects are expanded in console.log() (default 2)
root = "src"                        # root directory to discover tests from (default ".")
# preload = ["./tests/setup.ts"]    # scripts to run before each test file
# smol = false                      # reduce memory at the cost of perf (test-scoped)
# coverage = false                  # enable coverage reporting (--coverage overrides)
# coverageThreshold = 0.9           # fail if overall coverage is below this ratio (0-1)
# coverageSkipTestFiles = false     # exclude test files themselves from coverage stats
# coveragePathIgnorePatterns = [    # glob patterns to exclude from coverage
# coverageDir = "coverage"             # where lcov/persistent reports are written
# randomize = false                 # run tests in random order each time
# seed = 2444615283                 # fixed seed for reproducible random order (requires randomize = true)
# rerunEach = 0                     # re-run every test file N times (flaky-test detection)
# retry = 0                         # retry failed tests up to N times before reporting failure
# onlyFailures = false              # only display failed tests in output
# concurrentTestGlob = "**/concurrent-*.test.ts"   # files matching this glob run concurrently
# dots = false              # compact dot-per-test output instead of full names
# junit = "test-results.xml"  # emit a JUnit XML report to this path
# PACKAGE MANAGER  (bun install / bun add / bun remove)
production = false          # skip devDependencies, like --production flag (default false)
saveTextLockfile = true     # write text bun.lock instead of binary bun.lockb (default true since v1.2)
# exact = false             # save exact versions (e.g. "1.2.3") instead of caret ranges ("^1.2.3")
# frozenLockfile = false    # abort if lockfile would need updating (useful in CI)
# dryRun = false            # resolve & report without writing anything to disk
#                           #   "auto"     → install on-the-fly when node_modules is absent
#                           #   "force"    → always auto-install even if node_modules exists
#                           #   "fallback" → use node_modules first, auto-install missing packages
linker = "isolated"         # "isolated" → per-package installs (pnpm-like, default for new workspaces)
# linkWorkspacePackages = true   # symlink workspace packages into each other's node_modules
# globalBinDir = "~/.bun/bin"              # where global package binaries are linked (BUN_INSTALL_BIN)
# minimumReleaseAge = 259200    # only install package versions at least N seconds old (e.g. 3 days)
# minimumReleaseAgeExcludes = ["@types/bun", "typescript"]  # bypass list for the above
# Default npm registry (string or table form)
# cafile = "path/to/ca.pem"    # file may contain multiple certificates
# Security scanner plugin (must be installed as a dev dependency first)
# You can reference env vars with $VAR_NAME syntax.
disable         = false                         # skip reading from cache (may still write)
disableManifest = false                         # always fetch fresh manifests from registry
save  = true      # generate a lockfile on `bun install` (default true)
# print = "yarn"    # also emit a yarn-compatible lockfile alongside bun.lock
# Note: only the project-local bunfig.toml is read for [run]; global is ignored.
shell  = "system"   # shell used for package.json scripts
# bun    = false      # prepend PATH with a `node → bun` symlink for all scripts
#                     # equivalent to passing --bun to every `bun run` invocation
# silent = false      # suppress "Running <script>..." echo before each script
